correctness.rationale: Represent J_n as count of consecutive past observations below X_n, reading backward, before first larger: P(J_n=j)=1/[(j+1)(j+2)] for 0<=j<n and P(J_n=n)=1/(n+1). Given j, the destroyed current-record count equals independent reverse-rank records K_j=sum_{i<=j} Bernoulli(1/i); these insertion ranks have independent uniform laws. Summing A_j(z) gives (2-z)F_n(z)=1+(1-z)A_n(z)/(n+1), with cancellation at z=2 because A_n(2)=n+1. Subtract the geometric PGF 1/(2-z) to obtain P(G=k)-P(B_n=k)=[P(K_n+G=k)-a_{n,k}]/(n+1). Since A_n is real-rooted with all nonpositive roots, a_{n,k} is log-concave on 1..n; ratio of its convolution with geometric to a_{n,k} is nondecreasing in k, so signed masses cross once. Stochastic dominance then makes TV equal maximal CDF gap, the displayed geometric smoothing kernel and Kolmogorov gap. Uniform lattice LLT for independent Bernoulli with variance v_n=H_n-H_n^(2)~log n follows via Fourier bound |phi_n(t)|<=exp(-2v_n sin^2(t/2)); thus max a_{n,k}~1/sqrt(2pi v_n), and geometric smoothing attains the same asymptotically at k nearest H_n, giving sharp constant. Independently enumerated all permutations for n=1..6, matched exact mixture p(B2)=(1/2,1/3,1/6), and verified finite TV values. These finite checks do not prove LLT or n->infty.
